def can_make_increasing(n, m, a, b):
    # Flatten both matrices into lists
    flat_a = [x for row in a for x in row]
    flat_b = [x for row in b for x in row]

    # Sort both flattened lists
    sorted_a = sorted(flat_a)
    sorted_b = sorted(flat_b)

    # Create dictionaries to map original values to their sorted counterparts
    map_a = {val: sorted_val for val, sorted_val in zip(flat_a, sorted_a)}
    map_b = {val: sorted_val for val, sorted_val in zip(flat_b, sorted_b)}

    # Create new matrices based on the mappings
    new_a = [[map_a[a[i][j]] for j in range(m)] for i in range(n)]
    new_b = [[map_b[b[i][j]] for j in range(m)] for i in range(n)]

    # Check if both new matrices are strictly increasing
    def is_strictly_increasing(matrix):
        for row in matrix:
            if not all(row[i] < row[i + 1] for i in range(len(row) - 1)):
                return False
        for col in zip(*matrix):
            if not all(col[i] < col[i + 1] for i in range(len(col) - 1)):
                return False
        return True

    return "Possible" if is_strictly_increasing(new_a) and is_strictly_increasing(new_b) else "Impossible"
